about: What a software company may change in the Plait design. Protected: the scroll-run hero (threads from five sources tangle, braid through the product and come out as four lanes of work cards, then settle into the product window), the cost calculator's maths and week grid, the integrations browser, the seat pricing and its plan-that-fits logic, the workspace setup and its live preview, layout, type and all interaction code. The product's own words, sources, lanes, cards, numbers, integrations, plans and questions come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.

stages: the six steps of the hero, in order: the mess before (scattered), connecting the sources, sorting into lanes, threads becoming work items, work getting done, the calm after. Each has a short name, a caption and a clock time (Mon 9:14).

sources: five things the product pulls work from, each with a one- or two-character glyph. lanes: the product's four columns, the last one being done. cards: 8-16 example work items, each from a source (s, 0-4) in a lane (l, 0-3) with the owner's initials; at most four start in each lane, and one to three (not in the last lane) have ships: true and move to the last lane during the week.
demo: the example team's name and the hero's readouts, before and after: open items, tool switches, and hours a week given back.
integrations.items: each with a kind from integrations.kinds, what comes in, what goes back and how it syncs. start.preset: integrations (by name, among the first ten) ticked in the setup preview.
pricing.tiers: one to four plans, smallest first; price per seat a month (0 for free) and max seats, the last plan 0 (no limit). pricing.yearlyOff: the yearly discount in percent.
